denomProfiles/assyrian-church-of-the-eas: Modern heir of the ancient Church of the East, guardian of East Syriac worship.
The Christology of the Church of the East, which it describes as two natures united in one person.
The 1994 Common Christological Declaration with Pope John Paul II affirmed a shared faith in Christ.
Seven sacraments as the church reckons them, including the holy leaven and the sign of the cross.
Holds the Nicene Creed and the synods of the Persian church as normative.
Recognises Theodore, Diodore and Nestorius among its teachers.
Preserving Assyrian Christian identity and the Syriac language in the diaspora.
Ecumenical dialogue with the Catholic Church and other churches.
Rebuilding communities in northern Iraq and north-east Syria after war and displacement.
Theological education, such as the seminary revived in Erbil.
Holy Qurbana using the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, as well as those of Theodore and Nestorius.
Gregorian calendar adopted in 1964 (with Julian Easter elsewhere in some places).
Sacred leaven renewed each Holy Thursday.
Churches with plain interiors and the cross as the central symbol.
Ancient Church of the East
Separated in 1968 over the calendar and patriarchal succession.
Catholic–Assyrian relations
The 2001 Vatican guidelines recognised the validity of the Anaphora of Addai and Mari.
Mar Eshai Shimun XXIII (1908–1975)
Patriarch exiled in 1933; led the church from the United States
Mar Dinkha IV (patriarch 1976–2015)
Signed the 1994 declaration with Rome
Mar Gewargis III (patriarch 2015–2021)
Returned the patriarchate to Erbil
Mar Awa III
Patriarch since 2021, the first born in the United States
Its Archdiocese of India is the Chaldean Syrian Church based at Thrissur, Kerala, a small community whose metropolitan, Mar Aprem Mooken, became widely known as a writer.
denomProfiles/ancient-church-of-the-east: East Syriac traditionalists who kept the Julian calendar, based in Baghdad.
The same faith, Christology and liturgy as the Assyrian Church of the East.
Holds to the traditional Julian church calendar.
Rejected hereditary succession to the patriarchate.
Seven sacraments as reckoned in the East Syriac tradition, including the holy leaven.
Preserving East Syriac liturgy and the old calendar.
Pastoral care in Iraq and the diaspora (United States, Australia, Europe).
Dialogue on reunion with the Assyrian Church of the East.
Holy Qurbana of Addai and Mari in Syriac.
Feasts kept according to the Julian calendar, including Christmas on 7 January in the civil calendar.
Traditional East Syriac fasts and office.
Reunion discussions
Talks with the Assyrian Church from the 1990s onwards seek to heal the 1968 division.
Thrissur community
Part of the Chaldean Syrian Church in Kerala followed it between 1968 and 1995.
Mar Thoma Darmo (1904–1969)
Metropolitan in India who became its first patriarch in 1968
Mar Addai II (patriarch 1972–2022)
Led the church for half a century from Baghdad
Mar Gewargis III Younan
Patriarch since 2022
Its first patriarch, Thoma Darmo, had been metropolitan at Thrissur, and a section of the Chaldean Syrian Church there followed the Ancient Church until the factions reunited in 1995.
denomProfiles/lutheran/tagline: The churches of Luther's Reformation: justification by faith and Christ present in the sacrament.
denomProfiles/lutheran/coreDoctrines/0: Justification by grace alone through faith alone, on account of Christ (Augsburg Confession, art. 4).
denomProfiles/lutheran/coreDoctrines/1: Scripture is the norm of doctrine; the Book of Concord (1580) is its faithful exposition.
denomProfiles/lutheran/coreDoctrines/2: Law and gospel: God's word both accuses and promises.
denomProfiles/lutheran/coreDoctrines/3: Real presence: Christ's body and blood are truly given 'in, with and under' the bread and wine.
denomProfiles/lutheran/coreDoctrines/4: Baptismal regeneration and infant baptism; the priesthood of all believers alongside an ordained ministry.
denomProfiles/lutheran/coreDoctrines/5: The theology of the cross and the 'two kingdoms' doctrine of church and state.
denomProfiles/lutheran/focuses/0: Preaching the gospel and catechesis (Luther's Small Catechism, 1529).
denomProfiles/lutheran/focuses/1: Congregational song: the chorale tradition from Luther to Bach.
denomProfiles/lutheran/focuses/2: Education and literacy, including vernacular Bibles.
denomProfiles/lutheran/focuses/3: Diakonia: organised social welfare and relief, notably through the LWF.
denomProfiles/lutheran/focuses/4: Ecumenism, including the 1999 Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification with the Catholic Church.
denomProfiles/lutheran/practices/0: Liturgical Sunday Mass (Hauptgottesdienst) with sermon, creed and Eucharist, often weekly.
denomProfiles/lutheran/practices/2: Church year, vestments, altar and crucifix retained from medieval practice.
denomProfiles/lutheran/practices/3: Private confession and absolution, retained though less common today.
denomProfiles/lutheran/practices/4: Polity ranging from Nordic episcopal churches to synodical and congregational bodies.
denomProfiles/lutheran/influenced/0/text: Cranmer's reforms drew on Lutheran liturgy and teaching.
denomProfiles/lutheran/influenced/1/text: Shared justification by faith, while dividing over the Lord's Supper.
denomProfiles/lutheran/influenced/2/text: Renewed at Herrnhut in a Lutheran Pietist setting.
denomProfiles/lutheran/influenced/3/text: Wesley's heart was 'strangely warmed' hearing Luther's preface to Romans read in 1738.
denomProfiles/lutheran/influenced/4/text: Spener's Pia Desideria (1675) sought renewal within Lutheranism.
denomProfiles/lutheran/keyFigures/2/role: Chief architect of the Formula of Concord
denomProfiles/lutheran/members/note: Lutheran World Federation: over 77 million members in about 150 member churches; does not include non-member bodies such as the Missouri Synod.
denomProfiles/lutheran/inIndia: Indian Protestantism began with Lutherans: Ziegenbalg and Plütschau landed at Tranquebar in 1706; today some ten Lutheran churches, including the Tamil Evangelical Lutheran Church and the Gossner church of Jharkhand, form the United Evangelical Lutheran Churches in India.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/tagline: Sweden's former state church: Lutheran, episcopal and claiming apostolic succession.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/coreDoctr: Lutheran teaching as set out in the Augsburg Confession, adopted at the Uppsala Synod (1593).
Justification by grace through faith and the real presence of Christ in the Eucharist.
Episcopal order with bishops in historic succession.
Full communion with Anglican churches of the British Isles and Nordic-Baltic Lutherans through the Porvoo Communion (1996).
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/focuses/0: Serving the whole population as a 'folk church', from baptisms to funerals.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/focuses/1: International aid and mission through Act Church of Sweden.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/focuses/2: Ecumenism: Archbishop Nathan Söderblom convened the Life and Work conference in Stockholm (1925).
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/focuses/3: Progressive social stances, including women's ordination (1960) and same-sex marriage (2009).
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/practices: Sunday High Mass (Högmässa) using the church handbook, with chanted liturgy and hymnal.
Confirmation at around age 14, increasingly with camps.
Rich choral tradition and church music.
Funded by a church fee collected through the tax system for members.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/influence: Swedish mission (EFS) was among its founding influences.
Founded by Swedish Mission Friends emigrants in the United States.
Söderblom's Life and Work was a forerunner of the WCC.
The revival arose within the Church of Sweden in Lapland.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/keyFigure: Archbishop 1914–1931 and Nobel Peace Prize laureate (1930)
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/members/n: Church of Sweden statistics: about 5.5 million members, just over half the population.
denomProfiles/church-of-sweden/inIndia: The Church of Sweden Mission worked in Tamil Nadu alongside the Leipzig Mission, and Swedish bishops led the Tamil Evangelical Lutheran Church until Rajah B. Manikam became its first Indian bishop in 1956.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/tagline: Norway's Lutheran folk church, shaped by state ties and lay revival.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/coreDoctr: Lutheran confession: the Augsburg Confession and Luther's Small Catechism, with the ancient creeds.
Justification by faith and the real presence of Christ in the sacrament.
Episcopal order exercised with elected church councils and a General Synod.
A member of the Porvoo Communion with Anglican and other Nordic Lutheran churches.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/focuses/0: Serving as the national church while becoming independent of the state (constitutional change 2012; separate legal entity 2017).
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/focuses/1: Mission and aid through Norwegian Church Aid and mission societies.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/focuses/2: Lay organisations from the Haugean revival tradition.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/focuses/3: Debates over women bishops (from 1993) and same-sex marriage (liturgy adopted 2017).
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/practices: Sunday High Mass (høymesse) with Norwegian liturgy and hymnody.
High rates of baptism, confirmation and church funerals.
Strong prayer houses (bedehus) and lay mission meetings in rural areas.
Funded mainly by the state budget and municipalities.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/influence: Born from the Santal mission of Skrefsrud and Børresen.
Norwegian Missionary Society work in Madagascar from 1866.
Norwegian Lutheran Mission was a partner in southern Ethiopia.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/keyFigure: Bishop of Oslo who led church resistance to Nazi occupation (1942)
Presiding bishop since 2020, formerly WCC general secretary
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/members/n: Statistics Norway: about 3.5 million members, roughly 63% of the population.
denomProfiles/church-of-norway/inIndia: The Norwegian Lars Skrefsrud and the Dane Hans Peter Børresen founded the Santal mission at Benagaria in 1867, which became the Northern Evangelical Lutheran Church in Jharkhand, Bihar, West Bengal and Assam.
denomProfiles/evangelical-church-in-germ: Federation of Germany's Lutheran, Reformed and United regional churches.
Member churches confess the Lutheran, Reformed or United confessions, held together in one federation.
The Barmen Theological Declaration (1934) is a confessional text in many member churches.
Pulpit and altar fellowship between Lutherans and Reformed under the Leuenberg Agreement (1973).
Justification by faith and the centrality of Scripture as interpreted by modern scholarship.
Public theology: statements on ethics, peace, migration and social questions.
Diakonie: one of Germany's largest welfare organisations.
Coming to terms with the past, beginning with the Stuttgart Declaration of Guilt (1945).
Responding to steep membership decline and secularisation.
Sunday worship according to the regional church's agenda; Eucharist increasingly frequent.
Confirmation at about 14 and infant baptism.
Church tax collected by the state from members.
The biennial Kirchentag (lay church congress), founded in 1949.
Women ordained as pastors and bishops in all member churches.
Leuenberg Church Fellowship
Now the Community of Protestant Churches in Europe.
Missions in India and Africa
German mission societies (Leipzig, Gossner, Basel, Breklum) founded churches abroad.
Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod
Founded by Saxon emigrants who left in part over the union movement.
Friedrich Schleiermacher
Theologian who supported the Prussian Union
Karl Barth
Principal author of the Barmen Declaration
Dietrich Bonhoeffer
Confessing Church pastor and martyr
Martin Niemöller
Leader of the Pastors' Emergency League
EKD membership statistics: about 18.6 million members at the end of 2023.

German missions planted Lutheran churches in India: the Leipzig Mission in Tamil Nadu, the Gossner Mission among Adivasis of Chota Nagpur from 1845, and the Breklum Mission in Odisha (the Jeypore Evangelical Lutheran Church).
denomProfiles/lutheran-church-missouri-s: Confessional American Lutherans committed to the full Book of Concord and biblical inerrancy.
Unconditional (quia) subscription to the Lutheran Confessions in the Book of Concord.
Scripture is the inspired and inerrant Word of God.
Justification by grace through faith and the real presence of Christ in the Lord's Supper.
Ordained pastoral office restricted to men.
Fellowship only with churches in confessional agreement (close or closed communion).
Doctrinal faithfulness, exemplified by the 'Statement of Scriptural and Confessional Principles' (1973).
A large parochial school system and Concordia universities.
Theological education at Concordia Seminary (St Louis) and Concordia Theological Seminary (Fort Wayne).
Lutheran Hour radio broadcasts, begun in 1930.
International partner churches through the International Lutheran Council.
Liturgical worship from the Lutheran Service Book (2006).
Infant baptism, catechesis and confirmation.
Congregations call their pastors; the synod is an advisory association of congregations.
Communion restricted to those who share its confession.
Evangelical Lutheran Church in America
Seminex dissenters of 1974 formed the AELC, a founding body of the ELCA.
International Lutheran Council
A global association of confessional Lutheran churches.
India Evangelical Lutheran Church
Founded by Missouri Synod missionaries in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
C. F. W. Walther (1811–1887)
Founding president and theologian
Franz Pieper (1852–1931)
Author of Christian Dogmatics
J. A. O. Preus II (1920–1994)
President during the 1970s doctrinal conflict
Martin Chemnitz
Confessional authority much studied in the synod
Missouri Synod missionaries began work at Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, in 1895; the resulting India Evangelical Lutheran Church is strongest in Tamil Nadu and southern Kerala.
